# R262 — Native free grouped GEMM event-timing contract

Date: 2026-10-12 (JST). Read-only source and documentation review for WN `sync-xe-v0143-nonfinite-20261012` at immutable HEAD `0691bcdf`. No source changes, execution, compiler/build, import, test, device/process query, profiler, Git operation, or cleanup. This is a diagnostic design; no event timings were collected.

## Finding

The native grouped GEMM launch creates a SYCL command event internally, but Strata's production wrapper does not return it. `xmx_gemm_grouped` has a `void` API. Its selected route receives an event from the MMA grouped helper, DP4A grouped helper, or `parallel_for` for the XMX grouped functor, then passes that event to `finish` and drops it. With a non-null production stream, `finish` does not wait; the work remains asynchronous. `Gemm::f16_groups` is not an event-returning seam either. In a free build (`STRATA_ONEMATH=0`) it returns false, causing the caller to use the native grouped wrapper. Therefore no existing caller API supplies the exact grouped command event for direct kernel-service timing.

The production compute, transfer, and created stream queues are in-order queues without `enable_profiling`. Their events cannot be assumed to support `command_start`/`command_end` queries. The engine's timing event wrapper uses profiling tags or barriers and compares marker `command_end` values. Such markers are not the grouped kernel command, so their timestamp difference cannot be reported as that kernel's service time. Host wrapper elapsed time includes host and queue effects; it is a separate metric.

## Minimum diagnostic contract

Use a diagnostic-only profiling-enabled in-order queue on the same device/context and execute the exact production grouped call path, preserving the route predicates, arguments, bounds, geometry, and allocations. Select the actual production route at runtime and emit a route receipt (MMA, DP4A, or XMX grouped); do not infer XMX from a free build or the `f16_groups` name. The queue property changes the queue from production, so label measurements as profiling-queue diagnostics and later compare quiet end-to-end endpoints before treating them as production performance. Do not retrofit profiling onto or claim profiling support for an already-created production queue.

At the narrow launch boundary, return or capture the direct `sycl::event` from the selected launch together with the route identity. Keep the event alive through terminal completion and queries. After enqueue, record host-side submit and submit-to-completion intervals separately using a host steady clock. Call `wait_and_throw()` on the kernel event, run the runtime's asynchronous-error check, and require/query `command_execution_status == complete`. Then query `command_start` and `command_end` from that same kernel event; reject exceptions, missing values, or `end < start`. Report device command duration as `(command_end - command_start)` only. Keep raw device timestamps and host intervals in the receipt, plus device/runtime/compiler identity, queue profiling property, exact dispatch route, and workload/shape. Do not insert a barrier and subtract neighboring timestamps.

The diagnostic must create the queue with `property::queue::enable_profiling` from the outset and verify that the selected device/runtime supports queue profiling (including the SYCL profiling aspect where exposed). Querying profiling information on a non-profiling queue is invalid; the LLVM 7.1.1 headers also document `get_profiling_info` as potentially blocking until information is available. Explicitly wait and check errors first so asynchronous failure cannot be mistaken for a valid timing sample. Retain the event until all status and timestamp fields have been read.

This is event-timing eligibility, not proof of an XMX instruction, numerical correctness, sustained throughput, or an unperturbed production-queue time. Any inability to construct a profiling queue or query the event is a diagnostic failure, not a zero-duration sample. Keep command timing, host submit timing, and host completion timing in separate fields.

## Evidence and scope

Static source review found the following relevant boundaries: `src/prefill/gemm.cpp` (`Gemm::f16_groups`); `src/kernels/xe/xmx_gemm.cpp` (grouped route selection and `finish`); `src/core/device.cpp` (compute/transfer/stream queue construction); `src/core/gpu.cpp` (event marks and elapsed-time helper); `include/strata/core/runtime.hpp` (runtime event/queue interface). The installed LLVM 7.1.1 headers checked were `sycl/event.hpp` and `sycl/ext/oneapi/experimental/profiling_tag.hpp`.

Prior design context: R252 established the absence of a valid one-command free grouped FP16 device-event measurement; R256 established that the actual grouped route cannot be inferred from generic XMX eligibility; R146 requires separating per-command device time from host timing and comparing instrumented results with quiet endpoints. These prior reports are source/design evidence, not timing samples.

## Primary references

- Khronos SYCL 2020 specification, queue submission/event semantics and profiling: https://registry.khronos.org/SYCL/specs/sycl-2020/html/sycl-2020.html
- Intel oneAPI GPU Optimization Guide, kernel launch and event profiling: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/oneapi/optimization-guide-gpu/2024-1/kernel-launch.html
- LLVM 7.1.1 installed header: `.../install/include/sycl/event.hpp` (`wait_and_throw`, execution status, profiling-info behavior).
- LLVM 7.1.1 installed header: `.../install/include/sycl/ext/oneapi/experimental/profiling_tag.hpp` (profiling tag native event / fallback barrier behavior).
